best_architecture: Treat critique/reflexion as a closed verify-correct loop with FOUR strictly separated roles that should never be collapsed into one prompt: (1) Actor/Generator produces an initial output; (2) Evaluator/Verifier scores it against a rubric AND, critically, against EXTERNAL signals (unit tests, compiler, search/tool results, ground-truth, or a second model) rather than the model's own intrinsic judgment; (3) Self-Reflection module converts evaluation feedback into concise verbal lessons stored in episodic memory; (4) Refiner regenerates conditioned on prior output + reflection memory. The single most important design decision, supported by Huang et al. (ICLR 2024) and Gou et al. (CRITIC, ICLR 2024), is that the feedback signal must be EXTERNAL or DECOUPLED — intrinsic self-correction (a model grading its own reasoning with no external grounding) frequently fails to improve and can DEGRADE performance. Architect the loop so the evaluator has the strongest available oracle: deterministic checkers (test suites, type-checkers, JSON-schema validators, calculators, retrieval) first; LLM-as-judge only where no programmatic oracle exists, and then with a separate model instance, a structured rubric, and calibration against human labels. Chain-of-Verification's key structural insight applies broadly: FACTOR the verification — plan verification questions, then answer each INDEPENDENTLY without the original answer in context, so the model cannot just repeat its original (possibly wrong) reasoning. For tasks with no cheap oracle, prefer multi-agent debate (Du et al., ICML 2024) or Constitutional-AI-style critique-then-revise against an explicit written principle set, since a second perspective approximates external feedback. Operationally: bound iterations (typically 2-5), persist all intermediate states (actor output, evaluator verdict, reflection text) for observability, use a confidence/stop condition, and emit every step as validated structured JSON (Pydantic / JSON-schema constrained decoding) so the loop is machine-parseable and the evaluator's verdict is unambiguous. Memory should be a bounded sliding window of reflections (token budget), not unbounded accumulation.
reference_papers: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning (Shinn et al. 2023) - arXiv:2303.11366, NeurIPS 2023 - Actor/Evaluator/Self-Reflection with episodic memory; reinforces agents via linguistic feedback instead of weight updates; lifts HumanEval and decision-making/QA benchmarks

Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback (Bai et al. 2022) - arXiv:2212.08073 - critique-then-revise against a written 'constitution' (principle list); SL phase = self-critique+revise, RL phase = RLAIF with AI preference model; shows critiques before revisions beat direct revision

Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models (Dhuliawala et al. 2023) - arXiv:2309.11495, Findings of ACL 2024 - draft -> plan verification questions -> answer them INDEPENDENTLY (Factored variant) -> final verified answer; factored/decoupled verification prevents error propagation

Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate (Du et al. 2023) - arXiv:2305.14325, ICML 2024 - multiple LLM instances propose and critique each other's reasoning over rounds and converge; improves math/strategic reasoning and factuality; caveat: agents can converge confidently on a WRONG answer

Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (Huang et al. 2023) - arXiv:2310.01798, ICLR 2024 - landmark critique: INTRINSIC self-correction (no external feedback) often fails and can degrade accuracy; mandates external/oracle feedback in any critique loop

CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing (Gou et al. 2023) - arXiv:2305.11738, ICLR 2024 - Verify=>Correct=>Verify loop using external TOOLS (search, code interpreter) as the critique source; +7.7 F1 QA, +7.0% math, -79.2% toxicity; confirms tool/external feedback is essential

Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback (Madaan et al. 2023) - arXiv:2303.17651, NeurIPS 2023 - single LLM acts as generator+feedback+refiner over 3-step loop with feedback history in prompt; strong on code/style tasks for capable models; weaker where no good intrinsic signal exists

When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs (Kamoi et al. 2024) - arXiv:2406.01297, TACL 2024 - systematic taxonomy of when self-correction works vs. fails; reliable gains require external feedback, decomposed sub-tasks, or strong oracle verifiers

Encouraging Divergent Thinking in Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Debate (Liang et al. 2023) - arXiv:2305.19118, EMNLP 2024 - names and formalizes the Degeneration-of-Thought (DoT) problem (once confident, self-reflection stops producing novel thoughts even when wrong) and proposes tit-for-tat debate + judge as the fix; motivates the escalation path

Agent-as-a-Judge: Evaluate Agents with Agents (Zhuge et al. 2024) - arXiv:2410.10934 - agentic evaluator judges the full reasoning trajectory and intermediate artifacts (DevAI code-gen benchmark), aligning with human review better than output-only LLM-as-judge; basis for the Agent-as-a-Judge SOTA improvement

pitfalls: Relying on INTRINSIC self-correction with no external feedback: Huang et al. (ICLR 2024) show this often fails to improve and can DEGRADE accuracy. If Gemma's spec has the model critique its own reasoning with no oracle, that is the core anti-pattern — wire in tests/tools/retrieval/a separate judge.

Collapsing roles into one prompt: a model that generates, judges, AND revises in a single pass tends to rationalize its first answer. Use a SEPARATE evaluator instance and, for verification, answer verification questions WITHOUT the original answer in context (CoVe Factored).

Reflection poisoning: a wrong/biased critique steers the actor AWAY from a correct answer it already had. Always keep the best-so-far candidate, gate replacement on the evaluator's confidence, and never blindly overwrite.

Confident wrong convergence in debate (Du et al.): agents can agree on an incorrect answer and assert high confidence. Don't treat consensus as ground truth; keep an external check or a dissent/judge agent.
Unbounded loops / no stop condition: cost and latency blow up and outputs can oscillate. Bound iterations (2-5), add a satisfaction/confidence stop, and track marginal improvement.

Treating LLM-as-judge as a free oracle: judges have position bias, verbosity bias, self-preference bias and drift. They need structured rubrics, multiple passes, and calibration against human labels — and should be a fallback only where no programmatic checker exists.

No structured output contract: free-text verdicts are unparseable and ambiguous ('seems fine'). Force schema-constrained JSON (Pydantic / constrained decoding) with explicit pass/fail + actionable critique fields.

Naming it 'Constitutional AI' without an actual written principle set: CAI's power comes from an explicit, enumerated constitution the critic cites. A vague 'be better' instruction is not CAI and gives no auditable basis for the critique.
Unbounded reflection memory: appending all history overflows context and dilutes signal. Use a bounded sliding window / summarized reflections under a token budget.

Missing adversarial/red-team audit: a critique loop tuned only on the happy path won't catch jailbreaks, spec-gaming, or harmful outputs. Add an explicit adversarial auditor pass that probes for failure modes, not just quality scoring.

Degeneration-of-Thought (DoT): once the model is confident in its first answer, after ~3-4 self-critique iterations it converges and stops generating novel thoughts even when the initial answer is wrong (Liang et al. arXiv:2305.19118, the paper that named DoT). Beyond just keeping best-so-far, feed a FRESH external signal every round and add a convergence check that halts when revisions stop materially changing.

Sycophantic critic when the SAME model plays both Generator and Critic at similar temperature: the critic rubber-stamps the generator's output instead of finding genuine flaws (corroborated by SycEval and 'Challenging the Evaluator' arXiv:2509.16533). For Local-Claw's single-model two-persona design specifically, use a distinct adversarial critic system prompt, lower the critic temperature, ground in objective signals, and never reveal to the critic that it is judging its own output.

Structured critique schema ignored: the model emits issues_found:[] because it is reluctant to criticize, producing a hollow 'looks good' pass. Enforce a non-empty contract via Pydantic validation + Instructor re-ask, allowing an empty list ONLY with an explicit no_issues_justification field; treat unjustified empty critiques as a failed generation and retry.

Static critique on code that was never executed: critiquing a diff without running tests misses runtime bugs and invites hallucinated issues. For Local-Claw's code critique path, ALWAYS run the test suite / execute the code first and pass the results into the critic prompt — grounded critique, not speculative.
bdd_gherkin_scenarios:
Feature: External-feedback reflexion loop for code generation
  Scenario: Agent fixes a failing solution using test results as the oracle
    Given a coding task with a hidden unit-test suite as the external evaluator
    And the actor produces an initial solution that fails 2 of 5 tests
    When the reflexion loop runs with max_iterations = 3
    Then the evaluator returns the failing test names and error messages as external feedback
    And the self-reflection module writes a concise lesson to episodic memory
    And the refiner produces a new solution conditioned on the prior output and reflection
    And the loop stops as soon as all 5 tests pass or 3 iterations are reached
    And the final response and every intermediate state are emitted as schema-valid JSON

Feature: Chain-of-Verification factored fact-checking
  Scenario: Decoupled verification corrects a hallucinated claim
    Given a draft answer containing a factual claim
    When the critique agent plans a set of verification questions
    And each verification question is answered in isolation WITHOUT the draft in context
    And at least one verification answer contradicts the draft
    Then the agent regenerates a final answer that drops or corrects the unsupported claim
    And the JSON output includes the verification_questions, independent_answers, and a changed=true flag

Feature: Guard against intrinsic-only self-correction degradation
  Scenario: Loop refuses to overwrite a correct answer on weak self-critique
    Given the actor's initial answer is already correct
    And no external oracle (tests/tools/judge) is available, only intrinsic self-critique
    When the self-critique proposes a revision with confidence below the configured threshold
    Then the agent KEEPS the original best-so-far answer
    And records a warning that intrinsic-only correction was suppressed
    And does not degrade the output

Feature: Escalation from single-agent critique to multi-agent debate (Local-Claw)
  Scenario: A critical security finding triggers debate, routine findings do not
    Given the single-agent Generator/Critic loop reviews a code diff
    When the critic emits a Critique with severity = 'critical' and an issue of category 'security'
    Then the escalation_router initiates a multi-agent debate with 2 independent debaters and a judge
    And each debater must quote and rebut the other before the judge adjudicates
    And the final decision is taken from the judge's verdict
    And a Critique with severity 'low' or 'medium' bypasses debate and uses the single-agent suggested_revision

Feature: Constitutional violation detection in a writing draft (Local-Claw)
  Scenario: Unsupported claims populate constitutional_violations
    Given a writing draft containing factual claims with no cited evidence
    And a written constitution with task-specific writing-quality principles
    When the critique skill is invoked with critique_type = 'writing' and the constitution loaded
    Then Critique.constitutional_violations is non-empty
    And each violation references a specific constitutional principle id
    And suggested_revision either adds support for or removes each unsupported claim
optimal_implementation:
Implement four pluggable interfaces and one orchestrator.

  class Issue(BaseModel):
      location: str                       # file:line, paragraph, or reasoning-step id
      category: str                       # bug | style | factual | security | logic | clarity
      explanation: str
      grounded_by: str | None = None      # e.g. 'pytest:test_x failed', 'mypy:...'
  class Critique(BaseModel):              # structured verdict (Pydantic / JSON schema)
      verdict: Literal['pass','revise','fail']
      severity: Literal['low','medium','high','critical']   # drives the escalation_router
      score: float                        # 0..1
      issues_found: list[Issue]           # concrete, actionable (Local-Claw schema)
      constitutional_violations: list[str]# principle ids the output violates
      suggested_revision: str
      evidence: list[str]                 # external-feedback citations (test output, tool result, doc)
      confidence: float
      no_issues_justification: str | None = None  # required if issues_found is empty

  class Reflection(BaseModel):
      lessons: list[str]                  # bounded; what to change next attempt

  class Actor(Protocol):    def act(self, task, memory: list[Reflection]) -> Output: ...
  class Evaluator(Protocol):def evaluate(self, task, output) -> Critique: ...   # MUST use external signal when available
  class Reflector(Protocol):def reflect(self, task, output, critique: Critique) -> Reflection: ...

  Orchestrator loop (verify=>correct=>verify, CRITIC/Reflexion):
    best = None; memory = []
    for i in range(max_iters):
        out = actor.act(task, memory)
        crit = evaluator.evaluate(task, out)          # tests/tools/retrieval first; LLM-judge fallback
        best = out if (best is None or crit.score > best_score) else best   # keep best-so-far
        if crit.verdict == 'pass' or crit.score >= stop_threshold: break
        if escalation_router(crit):                    # severity=='critical' or any security issue
            return run_debate(task, out, crit)         # 2 independent debaters + judge
        if crit.confidence >= min_conf:                # guard vs reflection poisoning
            memory.append(reflector.reflect(task, out, crit))
            memory = memory[-MEMORY_WINDOW:]          # bounded episodic memory
    return best, trace                                # trace = all (out, crit, reflection) for observability

  def escalation_router(crit) -> bool:                 # single-agent default, multi-agent only for high-stakes
      return crit.severity == 'critical' or any(i.category == 'security' for i in crit.issues_found)

  Evaluator selection policy (key design rule): deterministic_oracle (unit tests / type-check / json-schema / calculator / retrieval-grounding) -> if none, separate-model LLM-as-judge with explicit rubric + factored CoVe verification -> if open-ended/no oracle, multi-agent debate or Constitutional critique against an explicit written principle list. Use constrained decoding (outlines/instructor) so Critique is ALWAYS valid JSON. For Constitutional mode: prompt = 'Critique the response against principle {p}; then revise' iterated over the constitution; store critiques (they outperform direct revision per Bai et al.). For debate mode: N actors answer, each sees others' answers + reasoning, revise for R rounds, aggregate by majority/judge; add a dissent agent to avoid confident-wrong convergence.
sota_improvements: Beyond a naive 'model critiques itself' loop Gemma may have planned, add: (1) Mandatory external-feedback gating — make programmatic oracles (tests, type-checkers, json-schema validators, calculators, retrieval) the PRIMARY evaluator and LLM-as-judge only a labeled fallback, directly addressing Huang et al. (2023) and Gou et al. (CRITIC, 2023). (2) Factored CoVe verification — answer verification questions decoupled from the draft to stop the model parroting its own errors. (3) Best-so-far retention + confidence-gated revision to prevent reflection poisoning. (4) Constrained-decoding structured critiques (instructor/outlines) so every verdict is schema-valid JSON, not free text. (5) Explicit written constitution / rubric the critic must cite, making critiques auditable (true Constitutional AI rather than vague 'improve this'). (6) A dedicated ADVERSARIAL AUDIT pass (red-team prompts probing jailbreaks, spec-gaming, harmful/unsafe outputs) distinct from quality scoring. (7) Multi-agent debate with a dissent/judge agent for open-ended tasks lacking an oracle, with safeguards against confident-wrong consensus. (8) Bounded episodic reflection memory (sliding window/summarized) under a token budget. (9) Full trace logging (LangSmith/Langfuse-style) of every actor/evaluator/reflection step plus judge calibration against human labels to detect drift. (10) Agent-as-a-Judge (Zhuge et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.10934) — have the evaluator judge the full reasoning TRAJECTORY and intermediate artifacts, not just the final output; aligns better with human review on code-gen (DevAI benchmark) and catches cascade failures single-output judges miss. (11) RLAIF distillation — distill the critique-revise traces back into the local Gemma model (Constitutional AI RL phase) so it internalizes critique quality and needs fewer runtime iterations, cutting inference cost on the A6000. (12) Tool-using structured verification — for code, actually EXECUTE the suggested_revision (apply patch + rerun tests) and only return it if it passes, rather than returning untested fixes. (13) Severity-gated escalation (single-agent default -> 2-debater debate only for severity=critical/security) to bound multi-agent cost on the local-inference budget.
